topic.title: Festive sales cost brands more to win
topic.claim: The Diwali sale you saw everywhere was less about demand and more about brands paying each other's price to be in front of you.
topic.behaviour: Every app, label and delivery service pushes festive ads at the same moment, so the same eyes get bid on by everyone.
topic.mechanism: When every brand bids for the same festive attention, the ad platform wins the auction. Brands pay a lot more to get a click and still see small sales growth.
topic.group: Marketers, founders and anyone who wonders why every ad looks the same in October
topic.moment: Every app you open in the Diwali week is showing you the same offer in a slightly different font.

turn.believed: Festive sales boom because everyone is spending more.
turn.actually: Brands are spending a lot more to get the same shoppers, and the sale itself barely moved.

topic.feeling: Bombarded, and a bit suspicious of every 'limited time' offer
topic.villain: An ad auction that rewards whoever bids the highest on the busiest days
topic.because: Platforms earn on every click, and brands cannot skip the festival. So the price of attention goes up while the buying pie hardly grows.

proof.fact: Criteo says online retail sales in the two weeks before Diwali were up 2% on the same period last year, while cost per click rose 62% and cost per thousand impressions 38% in that window. The article warns the figures come from Criteo alone and use different yardsticks.

topic.payoff: When everyone shouts at once, the loudest bill goes to the brand, and the shopper is the last person to find out.
topic.send_to: The marketing friend who still says Diwali is the best quarter
real_details: On Diwali day itself, CPC was up 83% and CPM up 65%.
topic.news_peg: On 16 November 2026 Criteo reported Diwali online sales up 2% year on year while festive ad costs rose sharply.
topic.why_now: The festive numbers are in and the gap between sales and ad cost is the story nobody sees in the feed.

score.why: The sale barely grew while the cost of shouting went up; the marketing friend is the obvious person to send it to.
